chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayyub, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who performed the obligatory prayer, and when he finished and raised his head from the second prostration of the fourth rak'ah, he broke his ablution. He said: As for his prayer, it has passed, and the Tashahhud remains; and indeed, the Tashahhud is a Sunnah in the prayer, so let him perform ablution and return to his seat or a clean place, and then perform the Tashahhud.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one breaks ablution after finishing the fourth rak'ah but before Salam?
ai.summary: In this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the distinction between obligatory pillars (fara'id) and recommended acts (sunan) clarifies that breaking wudu after the fourth rak'ah does not invalidate the prayer itself, as the core obligations have been fulfilled. The Imam instructs the worshipper to renew ablution and return to their place specifically to perform the Tashahhud, highlighting its status as a Sunnah in this specific context rather than a mandatory pillar that would require restarting the prayer. This reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that minor breaks in ritual purity after the main acts of prayer do not necessitate a complete re-performance of the Salāt.
